name: settings-nav
summary: The left navigation of a settings page: a small workspace label, then one row per page led by a colored icon tile, with the current page tinted, and an optional footer such as Sign out.
useWhen: An account or workspace has several settings pages, such as Profile, Plan, Usage and Security, and people move between them often.
Each page should be recognisable at a glance by a stable color and icon.

alternatives.name: tabs
alternatives.when: there are only two or three short views of one subject on a single page

alternatives.name: dropdown-menu
alternatives.when: the list of pages is a menu from an account button, not a persistent sidebar

rules.do: Give each page its own tile color and keep it the same wherever that page appears.
rules.dont: Color every tile the same, or swap colors between pages, so color stops meaning anything.

rules.do: Show the current page with the soft glass tint behind its row.
rules.dont: Fill the current row with lime; a lime block reads as a call to action.

a11y: It is a `nav` landmark named by its label. The current row carries `aria-current="page"`.
Rows are links when given an `href`, otherwise buttons; both show the lime focus ring.
Icon tiles are decorative; the row text names the page.
